content:
Someone on your Core Group may be able to serve for a known season. A move in the spring, follow-up through Launch Sunday, hosting for the next round of Vision Meetings. If the only yes you offer runs until you release them, they may decline. You lose help you could have used.

Agree on an intended last day, prepare the handover, and record the withdrawal when they actually leave. That date is a plan between the two of you. Everyfield will not end the commitment when the day arrives, and nobody has to sign again to remain committed. If they are still serving, the commitment stays active. This guide is for that conversation. Everyfield will not judge their calling, character, or fitness to serve, and it will not certify the exit.

---

## A planned last day is not an end date

A last day you agree on and a date that expires a record are not the same thing. Only the first belongs here.

Write the plan in your own notes, or in an optional note on their commitment. Plain words are enough. "Intended last gathering, June 14, then hand follow-up to Alex." That sentence tells you when to start the handover. It does not remove them from the Core Group.

Everyfield does not drop a commitment when a calendar date arrives, and it does not demand a new signature to keep someone in. A current commitment is active, withdrawn, or unknown. It changes when someone records an explicit dated withdrawal or a dated reactivation. A planned day does none of that.

<Callout type="important">
A date in your notes does not withdraw anyone. Record an explicit dated withdrawal when the person leaves. Until you do, the current commitment stays as it was, even if the planned day has passed.
</Callout>

If they are still serving, they are still committed. If they have left and the record still shows them as active, the count is wrong the other way. Fix that with a dated withdrawal. Do not hope a background rule will expire them for you.

---

## Name the season before they commit

The Three Key Documents already ask you to explain how long the Core Group phase lasts and what happens at launch. That phase length is the church's timeline. A personal season can be shorter. Say so before you ask for a signature.

Walk through the expectations with them, then ask what they can keep. Some people can stay through the move to Launch Team. Some can serve until a move, a job change, or Launch Sunday. A clear season is still a real yes.

The sample commitment language in that guide speaks of the duration of the Core Group phase. If that sentence is not their yes, say so before they sign. The card records the commitment they are making, including the intended last day you just named. It does not start a countdown.

Give them the same time to count the cost that you would give any other Core Group yes.

<Callout type="tip">
Say the shorter season out loud before they sign. If their yes runs only to a named day, that day should not be news at the first missed gathering.
</Callout>

---

## Write down what you both mean

You do not need a new form. You need a few sentences you can both find later. Label the date as a plan.

- [ ] Name the person and the work they will hold.
- [ ] Name the intended last day in words you both recognize.
- [ ] Name who will receive that work.
- [ ] Say that the date does not end the commitment by itself.
- [ ] Say how you will talk if they need to leave sooner or stay longer.
- [ ] Give both of you a copy.

Read it back. "You are committed now. We plan for your last gathering to be June 14. On that day we will record a withdrawal if you are leaving. If you are still serving, we will not withdraw you just because the date arrived."

That last sentence is the one people skip. Write it down.

| What happened | What the current commitment is |
| --- | --- |
| You agree on an intended last day | Active. The date is a plan, not an end. |
| The day passes and they are still serving | Active. Ask whether the plan has changed. |
| They leave and you record a dated withdrawal | Withdrawn. The current count goes down. The earlier commitment stays in the history. |
| You change their stage, or the Core Group becomes a Launch Team | Unchanged by that change alone. |
| They return and you record a dated reactivation | Active again. A return, not a first-time join. |

When the Core Group becomes a Launch Team, you may invite people to reaffirm commitment for the new phase. Core Group Commitments Explained treats that reaffirmation as optional. It is not a signature they must give to stay. A planned season does not pick up an expiry at that transition either.

---

## Hand the work over while they are still here

Most of a good exit is finished before the last day. Start while they can still introduce the next person and correct your guesses.

List the open duties. Follow-up with people they invited belongs on that list, along with any gathering they host, any training they lead, and any money task they hold. Do not leave those threads for the week after they are gone.

Introduce the next person in the room, not by a message the night before. Let the departing person explain how the work actually goes. Agree what the Core Group will be told, and who will say it. Ask, rather than announcing a reason they did not choose to share.

A stage change can prompt a handoff of open duties. Take that handoff. It still does not withdraw the commitment. Moving someone on the pipeline, or leaving a role, is a different act from recording that they have stepped out.

If no one can take the work, say that early. A planned exit with nowhere for the work to land is a staffing problem. It is not a reason to pressure them into an indefinite stay.

---

## Record the exit only when they leave

On the day they leave, record an explicit dated withdrawal. Use the day they actually stopped, not the day you first hoped they might. An old signature does not override that withdrawal. The person remains in your history. What changes is the current commitment.

Withdrawal lowers the number of adults currently committed. It does not erase the fact that they committed. If they come back, a later reactivation restores a current commitment. It does not create a new person, and it does not pretend the first commitment never happened.

Do not close the record on the planned day if they are still in the work. A calendar reminder is a prompt to talk. If you are unsure whether they have left, ask. A guess recorded as a withdrawal is worse than a short delay.

Everyfield will not make this call for you. It will not read attendance, silence, or a note and decide that their season is over.

---

## If the plan changes

Plans move. Have the conversation again.

If they need to leave sooner, hear the reason in private. Address the difficulty directly, and release them when that is what is needed. Thank them for the work they did. Record the withdrawal on the day they leave, and finish the handover as far as you still can.

If they want to stay past the planned day, let them. Ask what they are now willing to hold. Do not require a fresh signature to keep the commitment active. Update your note so the old date does not confuse the next leader. The new note is still a plan.

If the issue is harm, do not wait for the planned day. Follow your church's care and reporting duties. Everyfield does not judge fitness to serve. Your leaders still make that judgment.

Missed gatherings need that same private talk. Empty chairs can mean conflict. They can also mean sickness, shift work, or a school break. Attendance can say something about engagement. It cannot tell you the group is divided, and it cannot tell you this person has quit.

<Callout type="warning">
Do not withdraw someone because a week looked thin, and do not treat a smaller Core Group as a verdict on the plant. Ask what happened. Record a withdrawal only when they have actually left.
</Callout>

---

## Send them on their way

The last gathering should not be the first thank-you. Tell the Core Group what you agreed to tell them. Name the work the person did. Introduce whoever is taking it. Pray with them if they want that. Leave the door open for a return without making the return a new hoop.

If they come back later, welcome them and record a dated reactivation when they commit again. You do not need a new person record to make the count work.

<Callout type="scripture">
*"and they bore witness to your love before the church. You will do well to send them on their way in a manner worthy of God."* — 3 John 1:6 (LSB)
</Callout>

They know the day. Someone else knows the work. The record matches what happened. They leave with thanks, not with a silent drop off a list.

Wording: title is Planned Temporary Service and Healthy Exits, not the backlog title Term Commitments and Healthy Exits, so the heading does not sound like an expiring term. Slug follows that title: core-group/commitment/planned-temporary-service-and-healthy-exits.
Wording: sort_order 4 follows the published articles in core-group/commitment, which use 1, 2, and 3.
Wording: a planned last day may be written in human notes or an optional commitment note. That text is a plan only. It is not an enforced end date, and passing it does not withdraw anyone.
Wording: quoted 3 John 1:6 exactly as shown on read.lsbible.org on 2026-10-26, including the lowercase opening. Superscript cross-reference letters were not part of the prose and were omitted.
